correctness.rationale: For the explicitly defined aperiodic cyclic stochastic matrix with p_{N,k}=4(k+1)(N-k)/(N+1)^2, the characteristic equation is exactly product(1-delta/p_k)=1. Partial fractions yield S1=(N+1)H_N/2 and exact S2; endpoint estimates give S4=(N+1)^4 zeta(4)/128+O(N^3). The winding-one analytic root has |delta|/p_min=O(1/H_N), ensuring validity of the inverse log series even when max p_k~1. The leading inverse-series terms give the positive pi^4/(3(N+1)H_N^3) gap and negative pi^8/(90(N+1)H_N^5) correction with stated residual O(1/(NH_N^6)). The nontrivial global step compares modulus and argument on the product-modulus-one curve: for r>max q_k the argument increases monotonically as r decreases, so the first winding pair is subdominant. Direct eigenvalue matrices for N=20,35,60,100,180 independently corroborated the dominance and asymptotic scales; this finite evidence is not the infinite proof. Ratio of inverse gap to mean lap is 6H_N^2/pi^4 asymptotically.
residual_risks: Spectral gap alone yields lower worst-start total-variation mixing obstruction, not matching upper mixing bound in this nonnormal chain; does not certify coherent register preparation. O remainder is asymptotic not finite-N error bar.
